messages:
elaine: Heads up — getting a few customer reports where SSO logins are granting org-admin for a small % of users. Looks like a precedence bug in the JIT role mapper: tenant claim is being applied after role normalization and accidentally elevating privileges.

elaine: Repro steps we ran: 1) Okta assertion with claims below; 2) first login through JIT path; 3) user gets org-admin.

elaine: example SAML assertion (sanitized):
```
{
  "sub": "user-123",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "roles": ["viewer"],
  "tenant": "acme:org-admin",   # this is a namespaced tenant tag from idp
  "edupersonscopedaffiliation": ["member"]
}
```

elaine: Our mapper currently does: normalize roles -> map roles to RBAC -> apply tenant scoping. But in this case the tenant string contains an admin-suffix and we treat it as a role override. That leads to admin grant.

raj: ugh. can you paste the mapping config? which file handles precedence?

elaine: handler is at auth/jit/mapping.go, function ApplyClaimsOrder. current rules (simplified):
```
- merge roles array into set
- if roles empty, fallback to tenant-derived role
- apply tenant scoping
- enforce default least-privilege
```

elaine: bug is tenant parsing does a suffix match for "admin" and then writes into roles set after normalization. Should be sandboxed and require explicit allowlist.

alex: tagging @raj for SRE visibility. quick mitigation: drop tenant-derived role promotion in the JIT path and fallback to read-only. revertable in 5m.

maya: also seeing audit entries missing encryption context for the Okta assertion lookup in KMS logs. KMS decryption failures happened ~8:12am PST — might mean some assertions were processed with incomplete attributes.

elaine: good catch. stack trace from auth-service around 08:12:21: 
```
2025-05-04T08:12:21Z auth-service ERROR decrypt assertion: kms: decrypt failed: invalid encryption context
at auth/jit/crypto.go:47
```

elaine: hypothesis: two simultaneous issues — (1) precedence bug in mapping logic, (2) intermittent KMS context failures causing fallback codepath that trusts tenant claim differently. both combine to inflate few accounts.

raj: I'd like a quick rollout plan:
- immediate: patch mapping.go to never promote tenant-derived role without explicit allowlist (hotfix PR) :lock:
- immediate: revert any config that enables tenant-as-role in prod (flag off)
- audit: generate list of accounts granted org-admin since 08:00 and revoke if needed
- postmortem: deeper KMS investigation

alex: I'm on the hotfix PR now. will open branch and assign to eng-oncall for canary.

okta-bot: mapping-change-detected: rule_id=map-tenant-suffix created_by=admin.ops at 2025-05-04T08:10:02Z

elaine: okta-bot confirms change shortly before incidents — good signal.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for auth-service/hotfix-tenant-guard (3% hosts) :rocket:

maya: running audit query now:
```
SELECT user_id, created_at, granted_roles FROM audit_logs WHERE event='jit_grant' AND created_at >= '2025-05-04T08:00:00Z' AND granted_roles LIKE '%org-admin%';
```

maya: preliminary results: 7 distinct user_ids across 3 customers. notifying customer-success for outreach.

elaine: thanks. tagging @alex @raj — if canary looks clean we'll roll to 100%. Also add an immediate detection rule to alert on any new org-admin grants via JIT.

raj: created incident ticket SEC-2025-042 and assigned priority P1. adding audit owners and timeline.

alex: PR opened: github.com/redwood/auth/pull/1423 — patch enforces allowlist and adds extra KMS context checks. requesting review from @elaine and @maya.

elaine: reviewing now. also adding a unit test for tenant string parsing and an integration test that simulates KMS context failure.

maya: contacting KMS infra — they confirm some context rotation happened at 08:11 and some services received stale context. they're investigating rollback behavior.

okta-bot: idp-event: tenant-attribute-mapping-updated by admin.ops; audit_id=evt-87321

elaine: action items logged: 1) merge hotfix + deploy full rollback if failing; 2) revoke unintended admin grants and notify affected customers; 3) KMS postmortem; 4) tighten mapping allowlist and add detection.

raj: will run revocation script after deploy verification. sharing script in #eng-oncall.

alex: canary reports at +10m: no new admin grants, canary healthy. proceeding with staged rollout.

maya: KMS team found rotation script left a transient hole for ~90s. they are adding safety checks before rotation and will backfill missing contexts.

elaine: thanks team. keeping this thread updated. filing postmortem once all traces are collected. :rotating_light:
